mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here. Have you ever wondered why some people seem to naturally climb the ladder at work, while others—no less talented or driven—find themselves stuck, or quietly overlooked? Sometimes, it’s not the big moments that shape a career, but the quiet little habits we pick up along the way. Together, we're about to explore how the world of Nice Girls Don't Get the Corner Office—brought to life by Lois P. Frankel—shines a spotlight on those subtle patterns and social cues that many of us, especially women, have been taught to follow since childhood. You might be surprised to discover just how much those early lessons about being "nice" can sneak into our professional lives, sometimes holding us back more than we realize. As we walk through Frankel’s wisdom, we’ll look at how simple, everyday choices—from the way we speak, to how we sit in a meeting, or even the moments we choose to stay silent—can quietly shape the way others see us, and the opportunities that come our way. But here’s the exciting part: once we start recognizing these patterns, we open the door to real change. This journey isn’t about losing your authenticity—far from it. It’s about understanding which habits serve you, and which ones might be holding you back, so you can move forward with more intention, confidence, and influence. Let’s dive in together and uncover how small shifts can make a big difference in your career—and help you claim the recognition and leadership you truly deserve.
